# Checklist: security
<!-- Generated by /speckit.checklist -->
<!-- Branch: 005-gamificacao | Date: 2026-09-12 -->

Two new surfaces, both of which constitution Principle 5 makes **mandatory review**: the mission
photo upload, and the ledger as an audit trail. Plus the cross-tenant credit paths, because XP is
per organization and this is the first module that resolves a **global** identity to a **scoped**
one before writing to it.

## The mission photo (CLR-006, FR-036)

| ID | Check | Dimension | Ref | Status |
|----|-------|-----------|-----|--------|
| CHK021 | The submission stores a `midiaImagem` **id** — never a storage key, a URL or a filename. All four wrong shapes refused, and refused **before any write** | [input-sanitization] | FR-036, SC-017 | [ ] |
| CHK022 | The image belongs to the **same organization** as the submission (`sameTenant`), so a maker cannot attach a document of another lab | [authorization] | FR-036, FR-030 | [ ] |
| CHK023 | **A maker cannot attach another maker's media**, even within the lab. `scopedAccess` scopes to the lab and not the row — `Curtida.ts` and `PerfilMaker.ts` both record that gap for their own collections | [authorization] | FR-036 | [ ] |
| CHK024 | **What does a team member's browser render when it opens a stranger's upload in the review queue?** `midiaImagem`'s accepted MIME types decide whether an SVG can reach that page — an SVG is a document, and an inline one executes script | [data-protection] | FR-036, FR-021 | [ ] |
| CHK025 | The upload reuses 002's presigned PUT and **post-upload verification** unchanged — no second route, and the verification is not skipped because the owning collection is new | [input-sanitization] | D5, FR-036 | [ ] |
| CHK026 | A submission whose `comprovante` points at a media row that was later deleted — does the review queue crash, render a broken image, or refuse? | [error-states] | FR-036, FR-021 | [ ] |

## The ledger as an audit trail (CLR-008, FR-038)

| ID | Check | Dimension | Ref | Status |
|----|-------|-----------|-----|--------|
| CHK027 | **Append-only is enforced by ACCESS CONTROL, not by convention** — `update` and `delete` return `false` for a maker, for the team, and for a master. Asserted for all three, because "nobody would" is not a control | [authorization] | FR-001, D1 | [ ] |
| CHK028 | What can still erase history that access control does not cover — an admin bulk delete through `/admin`, a migration, a manual SQL fix? 002 named exactly those three as the paths `counters.ts` cannot see | [data-protection] | FR-001 | [ ] |
| CHK029 | CLR-008 accepts a trusted completion claim **because the ledger makes farming visible**. Does an entry carry enough to identify a farmer — who, which class, and a timestamp precise enough to show forty credits in four minutes? | [data-protection] | FR-038, SC-019 | [ ] |
| CHK030 | The claim CLR-008 makes is *bounded and auditable*, explicitly **not prevented**. Is that written where an implementer will meet it — beside the hook — or only in the spec? 004 learned a gap recorded only in a spec is a gap nobody meets again | [clarity] | FR-038, CLR-008 | [ ] |
| CHK031 | Deleting a maker's account (004 FR-031) leaves their ledger entries. Is that the intended answer for LGPD, given `docs/lgpd.md` states what deletion does, and does that document need a row for XP? | [data-protection] | FR-001, FR-012 | [ ] |

## Cross-tenant credit paths (FR-029, D3, D6)

| ID | Check | Dimension | Ref | Status |
|----|-------|-----------|-----|--------|
| CHK032 | **`perfilDoUsuarioNesta` is the first resolution from a global identity to a scoped profile.** Does it read through the tenant-scoped client, so a user with profiles at two labs cannot be resolved to the wrong one? | [authorization] | D3, FR-029 | [ ] |
| CHK033 | A team member of lab A approving content whose author is a profile of lab B — is that reachable at all, and if the content is scoped, what stops the *author relationship* from crossing? | [authorization] | FR-029, FR-030 | [ ] |
| CHK034 | The credit writes to `perfilMaker.xpTotal` of somebody who is **not** the requesting user. D6 verified `scopedAccess()` permits it. Is that verification recorded where the next reader will meet it, or will it look like a bug? | [authorization] | D6, FR-031 | [ ] |
| CHK035 | The `xp-ledger` isolation layer mutates `creditXp`'s **choice of client** (D7). Does mutating it actually produce a cross-tenant credit, or does some other guard catch it first and make the layer prove nothing? | [authorization] | FR-035, SC-010, D7 | [ ] |
| CHK036 | `/ranking` is the **first read in the product that deliberately returns other people's rows**. Every other scoped read returns the caller's own or published content. Is the confinement asserted, not assumed? | [authorization] | FR-037, SC-018 | [ ] |
